Eligibility: ABD certified/eligible; completed US ACGME or Canadian RCPSC-accredited dermatology residency by start
Application method: SF Match plus email personal statement, CV and three letters to fellowship director and administrator
Licence requirement: Eligible for and obtain a California medical licence
Summary: Two funded ACGME positions with outpatient and inpatient training, OR-based laser and procedural surgery and multidisciplinary clinics at Mt. Zion and UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital.

title: Dermatopathology Fellowship
Department: Department of Pathology (with Dermatology), UCSF
Duration: 2 years (first year ACGME-accredited, second year non-ACGME)
Deadline: FellowshipsCAS opens 1 October 2026; application deadline 15 January 2027 (for July 2028 start)
Eligibility: Completed ACGME residency in dermatology, AP-3 or AP/CP-4, or RCPSC-accredited equivalent in Canada
Application method: FellowshipsCAS and NRMP Match (from July 2028 starts)
Visa support: Department of Pathology may sponsor J-1 visas; non-US citizens need permanent residence or appropriate educational visa
Summary: A two-year dermatopathology programme with an academic orientation, built on a high-volume service with a large proportion of challenging consultation material.

title: Dermatopathology Fellowship
Department: Department of Dermatology (Yale Dermatopathology)
Duration: 1 year (optional second research year depending on funding)
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Application method: Fellowship application form, CV, photo, diploma, personal statement and three reference letters
Summary: One-year ACGME dermatopathology training with one of the largest academic dermatopathology groups in the US.

title: Dermatopathology Fellowship
Department: Department of Dermatology, Perelman School of Medicine
Deadline: Page states applications for July 2027–June 2028 were accepted 1 June – 1 August 2025 (21 months before start); check for the current cycle
Eligibility: Board eligible/certified in dermatology or pathology
International applicants: IMGs submit ECFMG documentation where applicable
Application method: Online application form with CV, personal statement, 3 letters, transcripts, dean's letter and USMLE/ECFMG reports
Summary: A fully approved programme within the Department of Dermatology offering diagnostic dermatopathology, immunodermatology, clinical correlation and research.

title: Dermatopathology Fellowship
Department: Departments of Dermatology and Pathology, Feinberg School of Medicine
Deadline: FellowshipsCAS opens 1 October 2026 for the 2028–2029 fellowship
Eligibility: Pathologists or dermatologists
Application method: ASDP fellowship match via FellowshipsCAS
Summary: A joint dermatology–pathology ACGME fellowship providing subspecialty competence in dermatopathology with research and teaching expected.

title: Dermatopathology Fellowship
Department: Departments of Pathology and Dermatology
Eligibility: AP/CP, AP or dermatology board-eligible
Application method: FellowshipsCAS; NRMP Pathology Fellowship Match
Funding: Generous annual educational stipend and research support
Summary: A one-year ACGME fellowship in a busy, high-volume complex dermatopathology practice at Cedars-Sinai.

title: Pediatric Dermatology Fellowship
inst: Washington University in St. Louis / St. Louis Children's Hospital
Department: Division of Dermatology, Washington University School of Medicine
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Application method: SF Match; CV, two letters of recommendation and personal statement
Summary: Broad training in outpatient, inpatient consult, procedural/laser paediatric dermatology and research at St. Louis Children's Hospital, including vascular anomalies and paediatric melanoma clinics.

title: Pediatric Dermatology Fellowship
Department: Section of Dermatology, Children's Hospital of Philadelphia
Eligibility: Completion of a recognised dermatology residency
Application method: SF Match; request application from programme coordinator by email
Summary: Prepares fellows to care for complex medical and surgical paediatric dermatology patients, with an expected research project to jump-start an academic career.

title: Pediatric Dermatology Fellowship
inst: Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital / Northwestern University
Department: Division of Dermatology, Department of Pediatrics, Feinberg School of Medicine
Eligibility: Board eligible or certified in dermatology before starting
Application method: Contact programme; submit CV, three letters and headshot; register with SF Match (match in November)
Licence requirement: Eligible for a temporary Illinois medical licence
Summary: Scientific opportunities and broad clinical training in paediatric dermatology at Lurie Children's Hospital, with one to two publications encouraged during the year.

title: Pediatric Dermatology Fellowship
inst: Columbia University Irving Medical Center / NewYork-Presbyterian
Department: Department of Dermatology, Columbia University
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Application method: Not stated on official page
Summary: Advanced training at NewYork-Presbyterian Morgan Stanley Children's Hospital for dermatologists seeking expertise in complex paediatric skin disease and academic leadership.

title: Mohs Surgery Fellowship
inst: Women's College Hospital, University of Toronto
Department: Division of Dermatology, Department of Medicine, University of Toronto
Eligibility: Completed full dermatology residency by fellowship start
Accreditation: ACMS-accredited fellowship; University of Toronto postgraduate training
Application method: SF Match (Mohs surgery match)
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a CPSO certificate authorizing postgraduate education (educational licence); IMGs complete a Pre-Entry Assessment Program
Summary: An ACMS-accredited fellowship at Women's College Hospital with three Mohs surgeons performing about 3,000 cases a year and close collaboration with oculoplastic, plastic and head-and-neck surgeons.

title: Advanced Medical Dermatology Fellowship
Department: Division of Dermatology, Department of Medicine, University of Toronto
Eligibility: Fully trained and certified dermatologists
International applicants: Not stated on official page (open to certified dermatologists subject to CPSO licensure)
Accreditation: University of Toronto clinical fellowship (Certificate of Completion); does not lead to RCPSC certification
Application method: Contact programme administrator
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a CPSO certificate authorizing postgraduate education (educational licence); IMGs complete a Pre-Entry Assessment Program
Summary: Training in the management of severe systemic dermatological disease such as CTCL and pemphigus variants, with preference for future academics and those pursuing a graduate degree.

title: Dermatologic Laser Surgery and Aesthetic Dermatology Fellowship
Department: Division of Dermatology, Department of Medicine, University of Toronto
Deadline: Applications open 1 October to 30 September of the following year
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
Accreditation: University of Toronto clinical fellowship (Certificate of Completion); does not lead to RCPSC certification
Application method: Contact fellowship supervisors
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a CPSO certificate authorizing postgraduate education (educational licence); IMGs complete a Pre-Entry Assessment Program
Summary: Develops expertise in cutaneous lasers and energy-based devices and aesthetic procedures including fillers, biostimulators, neuromodulators and sclerotherapy, with research expected.

title: Pediatric Dermatology Fellowship
Department: Division of Allergy, Immunology and Dermatology, Department of Pediatrics, McGill University
Eligibility: English and French required
Application method: McGill PGME fellowship application
Funding: Candidates must secure funding to apply (bursary information via Department of Pediatrics)
Summary: A one-year clinical fellowship at the Montreal Children's Hospital and Crowley Clinic developing expertise in complex and common paediatric skin disease, including vascular anomalies and paediatric dermatologic surgery.

title: Laser Medicine and Photobiology Clinical Fellowship
Department: Department of Dermatology and Skin Science, UBC
Eligibility: Post-residency trainee who has completed requirements for registration as a dermatologist in their home country
International applicants: Yes — past clinical fellows have come from Canada and many other countries
Application method: Arranged directly with the supervising faculty member
Summary: A one-to-one mentored clinical and research fellowship in laser medicine and photobiology positioning fellows for academic or practising careers.

title: Immunodermatology Clinical Fellowship
Department: Department of Dermatology and Skin Science, UBC
Eligibility: Post-residency trainee who has completed requirements for registration as a dermatologist in their home country
International applicants: Yes — past clinical fellows have come from Canada and many other countries
Application method: Arranged directly with the supervising faculty member
Summary: A one-to-one mentored clinical and research fellowship in immunodermatology within UBC's Department of Dermatology and Skin Science.

title: ACD Mohs Surgery Training Fellowship – The Skin Hospital Westmead
Department: Australasian College of Dermatologists (ACD) accredited Mohs Surgery Training position
Eligibility: FACD or equivalent international dermatology qualification and licensed to practise as a dermatologist in Australia, or ACD advanced trainee with full AHPRA registration
International applicants: Internationally trained dermatologists should first have skills assessed as substantially comparable to Australian-trained dermatologists
Application method: ACD online application form
Licence requirement: AHPRA registration / licence to practise as a dermatologist in Australia
Summary: An ACD-accredited Mohs surgery training position at The Skin Hospital Westmead providing advanced competence in Mohs surgery, histopathological interpretation and reconstruction.

title: ACD Mohs Surgery Training Fellowship – Skin Health Institute
Department: Australasian College of Dermatologists (ACD) accredited Mohs Surgery Training position
Eligibility: FACD or equivalent international dermatology qualification and licensed to practise as a dermatologist in Australia, or ACD advanced trainee with full AHPRA registration
International applicants: Internationally trained dermatologists should first have skills assessed as substantially comparable to Australian-trained dermatologists
Application method: ACD online application form
Licence requirement: AHPRA registration / licence to practise as a dermatologist in Australia
Summary: An ACD-accredited Mohs surgery training position at the Skin Health Institute providing advanced competence in Mohs surgery, histopathological interpretation and reconstruction.

title: Oncodermatology Fellowship
Department: Department of Dermatology, Westmead Hospital
Eligibility: Dermatologists who have completed their training
Application method: Not stated on official page
Funding: Honorary (unpaid) position; candidates bring their own sponsorship
Summary: A one-year honorary programme with keratinocyte carcinoma, high-risk melanoma, transplant, cutaneous lymphoma and GVHD clinics plus melanoma and skin cancer MDTs (no Mohs training).

title: Post-CCT Fellowship in Mohs and Advanced Dermatological Surgery (NHS Jobs advert)
inst: Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (Royal Victoria Infirmary)
Department: Department of Dermatology, Royal Victoria Infirmary
Start: August 2026 (advert posted 16 February 2026; check for next cycle)
Eligibility: Substantive dermatologists, trainees within six months of CCT, or immediately post-CCT
Accreditation: Newcastle (RVI) is a BAD/BSDS-accredited Post-CCT Mohs fellowship site
Application method: NHS Jobs
Visa support: Skilled Worker sponsorship applicants welcome (per NHS Jobs advert)
Summary: A one-year fellowship for advanced training in Mohs micrographic surgery, reconstruction, scar revision, lasers and cutaneous oncology at the RVI Newcastle.

title: Senior Clinical Fellowship in Paediatric Dermatology (NHS Jobs advert)
inst: Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust (Nottingham Children's Hospital)
Department: Paediatric Dermatology, Queen's Medical Centre
Start: Advert posted 2 February 2026; check for next cycle
Eligibility: Preference for those meeting CCT requirements in dermatology; also pre-CCT/CESR trainees or paediatricians; minimum 1 year specialised paediatric dermatology experience; MRCP or MRCPCH
Accreditation: Accredited by the British Association of Dermatologists for post-CCT fellowship training
Application method: NHS Jobs
Visa support: Skilled Worker sponsorship applicants welcome (per NHS Jobs advert)
Summary: Twelve months of supervised experience in paediatric dermatology, general paediatrics as applied to dermatology, and advanced paediatric dermatology and genetics.
